nodes.intent: where the party is put ashore and where the works first shows itself
nodes.note: The shingle under the north cliff. The works stands above and south; the light on the headland is one spark at the far end of the sight.

nodes.intent: the lower pans the sea took, crossed at low water
nodes.note: Six evaporating pans with their walls broken. Crossing it is the first cost the delve charges.

nodes.intent: the last shed standing on the pans, and the first shelter
nodes.note: Low, salt-eaten, a door at each end. The first place a body stands out of the wind.

nodes.intent: the cut stair off the pans, climbing the face to the works
nodes.note: Cut by the same hands that cut the brine gallery above it.

nodes.intent: the rock-cut gallery that carried brine up to the pans
nodes.note: Pipe cradles still bolted to the rock. It is the works' own throat.

nodes.intent: the great boiling house, the building the delve is named after
nodes.note: Four lead pans over four furnaces under a clerestory the whole length of it. The one interior with height.

nodes.intent: the stoking walk behind the furnaces
nodes.note: Black and close, directly behind the fires the boiling house is heated by.

nodes.intent: the yard where coal was landed and stacked
nodes.note: Open to the sky, walled to the sea. Where the works met the world.

nodes.intent: the hoist that lifted coal from the yard to the store
nodes.note: A narrow tower with its wheel still in it: the works' one vertical interior.

nodes.intent: the dry store where finished salt was kept
nodes.note: High windows down the long wall, floor swept to bare stone. The driest room on the site.

nodes.intent: the barrel shop that packed the salt
nodes.note: Half-made casks on the bench and hoops on the wall.

nodes.intent: the yard the works and the abbey share, and the hinge of the map
nodes.note: Everything walked so far opens onto it, and the abbey gate stands across it.

nodes.intent: the abbey gatehouse, barred from the inside
nodes.note: The one way into the precinct, and the delve's first held door.

nodes.intent: the garth the abbey buildings stand around
nodes.note: Open to the sky, walks on four sides, a well in the middle gone to salt.

nodes.intent: the north walk, the covered route between the abbey rooms
nodes.note: Arcaded on the garth side: the abbey's one way of letting light in, repeated the length of it.

nodes.intent: the chapter house, where the party can rest
nodes.note: Stone bench round the wall, one high window, and nothing that can reach in.

nodes.intent: the refectory, where the community ate and where it stopped
nodes.note: Tables still laid. What happened here is the delve's middle revelation.

nodes.intent: the abbey church, the tallest thing on the headland after the light
nodes.note: Clerestory windows both sides, the same rhythm as the boiling house. One hand built both.

nodes.intent: the undercroft beneath the church, where the abbey kept what it would not say
nodes.note: Reached by a stair off the church floor. Low, dry, and the only place the delve goes down.

nodes.intent: the prior's lodging, the last room anyone lived in
nodes.note: A bed, a desk, and a ledger nobody closed.

nodes.intent: the night stair head, where the precinct ends and the headland begins
nodes.note: Built so the community could reach the light in the dark without going outside.

nodes.intent: the exposed path along the headland to the light
nodes.note: No cover, sea on both sides. From here the whole site reads as one silhouette.

nodes.intent: the walled court at the foot of the light, where the delve is decided
nodes.note: Walled to keep the weather off the fuel, which is what makes it a room and not a clifftop.

nodes.intent: the lantern room at the top of the light
nodes.note: The last place. Whoever has been tending it has been standing here.
